ucs.title: [LLM] Black Basta / Storm-1811 Quick Assist vishing → remote-access tool drop
ucs.description: Hunts Microsoft Quick Assist (quickassist.exe) spawning LOLBins or remote-access tool installers (AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, NetSupport, Splashtop, Atera). This is the signature post-vishing chain Microsoft tracks as Storm-1811 / Black Basta affiliates — operators email-bomb the victim, call posing as IT support via external Teams chat, talk the user into launching Quick Assist, then push a RAT installer that becomes the beachhead for SystemBC / Cobalt Strike and ultimately Black Basta ransomware.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="quickassist.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","msiexec.exe","rundll32.exe","AnyDesk.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","client32.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","TeamViewer.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*anydesk*","*screenconnect*","*connectwise*","*netsupport*","*splashtop*","*atera*","*\\Downloads\\*.msi","*\\Downloads\\*.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user, "\$$") AND NOT match(user, "(?i)^(system|local service|network service)$") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "quickassist.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","msiexec.exe","rundll32.exe","AnyDesk.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","client32.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","TeamViewer.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("anydesk","screenconnect","connectwise","netsupport","splashtop","atera")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has "quickassist.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","msiexec.exe","rundll32.exe","AnyDesk.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","client32.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","TeamViewer.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("anydesk","screenconnect","connectwise","netsupport","splashtop","atera")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActorUsername !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Quick Assist Spawning Remote-Access Tool or LOLBin (Black Basta / Storm-1811)
id: 7c8b3f9a-2d4e-4a1b-9c3d-1f2e3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Quick Assist spawning RAT installers, LOLBins, or downloaders associated with Black Basta / Storm-1811 vishing operations
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2024/05/15/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/
author: SOC detection engineering
date: 2026/05/29
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\quickassist.exe'
  selection_child_lolbin:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_child_rat:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'anydesk'
      - 'screenconnect'
      - 'connectwise'
      - 'netsupport'
      - 'splashtop'
      - 'atera'
  condition: selection_parent and (selection_child_lolbin or selection_child_rat)
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Microsoft Support remote sessions (uncommon and easily verified)
level: high
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1566.004
  - attack.t1204.002
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\quickassist.exe OR *\\QuickAssist.exe OR *\\QUICKASSIST.EXE) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\CertUtil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*anydesk* OR *AnyDesk* OR *ANYDESK* OR *screenconnect* OR *ScreenConnect* OR *connectwise* OR *ConnectWise* OR *netsupport* OR *NetSupport* OR *splashtop* OR *Splashtop* OR *atera*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/quickassist\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|curl|certutil|bitsadmin|mshta|msiexec|rundll32)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(anydesk|screenconnect|connectwise|netsupport|splashtop|atera)/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ucs.rationale: Quick Assist (quickassist.exe) is the linchpin of Microsoft Storm-1811 / Black Basta's 2024-2025 social-engineering chain documented by Microsoft Threat Intelligence (and corroborated by Rapid7 / ReliaQuest IR reports). Quick Assist is rarely launched legitimately, and when it IS, it almost never spawns LOLBins or RAT installers — that combination is essentially pathognomonic for this actor's TTP

ucs.title: [LLM] Black Basta LSASS dump → SMB admin-share write → PsExec lateral chain
ucs.description: Hunts the characteristic Black Basta post-access tradecraft: dump LSASS with comsvcs.dll MiniDump or ProcDump for credentials (T1003.001), then within ~2h write a payload to a remote host's C$/ADMIN$ share (T1021.002) and trigger execution via PsExec / a remote service (T1569.002). Chains the three signature TTPs into a single high-confidence verdict that lone LSASS dumps or lone SMB writes can't deliver.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t min(_time) as dump_time values(Processes.process) as dump_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*" AND Processes.process="*MiniDump*") OR (Processes.process="*procdump*" AND Processes.process="*lsass*") OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*MiniDump*") OR Processes.process="*lsass.dmp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename dest as dump_host | join type=inner user [ | tstats summariesonly=t min(_time) as smb_time values(Filesystem.file_path) as smb_paths values(Filesystem.file_name) as smb_files from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\\\*\\C$\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\\\*\\ADMIN$\\*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("PSEXESVC.exe","PsExec.exe","paexec.exe","csrss.exe","servicedll.dll")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as target_host ] | where smb_time >= dump_time AND smb_time <= dump_time + 7200 AND dump_host != target_host | eval delta_sec = smb_time - dump_time | table dump_time smb_time delta_sec user dump_host target_host smb_paths smb_files dump_cmd | sort - dump_time
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSec = 7200;
let LsassDumps =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where (FileName =~ "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "comsvcs.dll" and ProcessCommandLine has "MiniDump")
        or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("procdump", "lsass"))
        or ProcessCommandLine has "lsass.dmp"
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project DumpTime = Timestamp, SrcHost = DeviceName, AccountName, DumpCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
let AdminShareWrites =
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\C$\", @"\ADMIN$\")
        or FileName in~ ("PSEXESVC.exe","PsExec.exe","paexec.exe","servicedll.dll")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project SmbTime = Timestamp, DstHost = DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              TargetPath = FolderPath, FileName,
              WriterProc = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              WriterCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
LsassDumps
| join kind=inner AdminShareWrites on AccountName
| where SmbTime between (DumpTime .. DumpTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| where SrcHost != DstHost
| project DumpTime, SmbTime,
          DeltaSec = datetime_diff('second', SmbTime, DumpTime),
          AccountName, SrcHost, DstHost, TargetPath, FileName, DumpCmd, WriterProc, WriterCmd
| order by DumpTime desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSec = 7200;
let LsassDumps =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and CommandLine has "comsvcs.dll" and CommandLine has "MiniDump")
        or (CommandLine has "procdump" and CommandLine has "lsass")
        or CommandLine has "lsass.dmp"
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project DumpTime = TimeGenerated, SrcHost = Computer, AccountName = SubjectUserName, DumpCmd = CommandLine;
let AdminShareWrites =
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\C$\", @"\ADMIN$\")
        or TargetFileName in~ ("PSEXESVC.exe","PsExec.exe","paexec.exe","servicedll.dll")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project SmbTime = TimeGenerated, DstHost = DvcHostname,
              AccountName = ActorUsername,
              TargetPath = TargetFilePath, FileName = TargetFileName,
              WriterProc = ActingProcessName,
              WriterCmd  = ActingProcessCommandLine;
LsassDumps
| join kind=inner AdminShareWrites on AccountName
| where SmbTime between (DumpTime .. DumpTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| where SrcHost != DstHost
| project DumpTime, SmbTime,
          DeltaSec = datetime_diff('second', SmbTime, DumpTime),
          AccountName, SrcHost, DstHost, TargetPath, FileName, DumpCmd, WriterProc, WriterCmd
| order by DumpTime desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDLL32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE) @CommandLine:(*comsvcs.dll* OR *COMSVCS.DLL*) @CommandLine:(*MiniDump* OR *minidump* OR *MINIDUMP*)) OR (@CommandLine:(*procdump* OR *ProcDump* OR *PROCDUMP*) @CommandLine:(*lsass* OR *LSASS*)) OR @CommandLine:(*lsass.dmp* OR *LSASS.DMP*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/rundll32\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/comsvcs\.dll/i AND CommandLine=/minidump/i) OR (CommandLine=/procdump/i AND CommandLine=/lsass/i) OR CommandLine=/lsass\.dmp/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\(C|ADMIN)\$\\/i OR TargetFileName=/(PSEXESVC|PsExec|paexec|servicedll)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=min(_time))}, field=UserName, include=[TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName])
| groupBy([UserName, ComputerName, aid, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())
ucs.rationale: Black Basta IR write-ups (CISA #StopRansomware advisory AA24-131A, Mandiant, ReliaQuest) consistently show the same operator playbook: dump LSASS (often via the comsvcs.dll MiniDump LOLBAS trick to evade Defender's procdump signature), reuse the harvested creds over SMB to push a payload to ADMIN$/C$ on additional hosts, then trigger execution via PsExec / a remote service before final ransomware
